findings.evidence: `grep skewProd|shear code/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Orientation` gives no hits, so no public form exists. `Orientation.prod` and `map_prod` live in `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Orientation/Prod.lean:83,260`, and `kerOfExact`/`map_ofExact` in `Orientation/Exact/Basic.lean:220,336`, so every dependency is linear algebra.
findings.fix: Move it into `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Orientation/Prod.lean` as a public lemma, e.g. `Orientation.map_skewProd_refl_prod`. Ideally generalize it to `e₁.skewProd e₂ f` acting on `o.prod p` for any `f`, and use it from here.
findings.issue: `map_shear_orientation` is general infrastructure hidden as `private`. Its statement mentions only linear-algebra objects (`Orientation.map`, `LinearEquiv.skewProd`, `Orientation.prod`), and its proof does not depend on manifolds or the diagonal. It states that the shear `(a, b) ↦ (a, a + b)` preserves the product orientation.

findings.evidence: Line 42 `abbrev diagonal : SmoothEmbedding I (I.prod I) ∞ M (M × M) where ...`. Lines 48–55 already provide the simp characterization `diagonal_apply` / `coe_diagonal`.
findings.fix: Make it a plain `def`, without `@[expose]`, and keep `diagonal_apply`/`coe_diagonal` as the interface (proved with `(rfl)`). Add a lemma for any other unfolding a consumer needs.
findings.issue: `diagonal` is declared as an `abbrev` in a public section. That exposes its body and makes it reducible, so downstream code can depend on its definitional unfolding even though `diagonal_apply` and `coe_diagonal` already characterize it.

summary: A general linear-algebra orientation lemma is hidden as `private` in a manifold file instead of being made public in its canonical home. `diagonal` is an `abbrev`, which exposes and reduces its body downstream even though apply lemmas already characterize it.
